text: Zither HarpHi, everyone.Nice to see you here.I'm Lulu.Before starting the lesson, please make sure you have got everything ready.In today's lesson, we are going to talk more about encyclopedia articles.Is a printed encyclopedia a useful reference book in your mind?What's your view, Joyce?I think printed encyclopedias are still useful today.It is a good idea to read encyclopedias for information we need.We can easily find what we want.They can enrich our knowledge.Do you agree, Lucas?I prefer to use the Internet.It's quick and convenient.You just need to type in the keywords and piles of information are just inside.All you need to do is select what you want.But sometimes, the information you get from the Internet is full of mistakes.You have to tell which is right and which is wrong.It takes time.The encyclopedia gives the true facts.They are a reliable source for information.I have to say it's true.There are debates on whether we still need paper encyclopedias or not.But I believe reading is a good habit.At least, when you need to step high, a sick encyclopedia is a good helper, isn't it?Just kidding.Look at the picture in the top right corner.It is called the Britannica.It is the best-known encyclopedia in the world.It is also the bestseller.Nowadays, we can use the Britannica online, but you need to pay.The Britannica is sometimes hard to understand.Most readers are adults.For children, we can read children's encyclopedias.They are easy to read and understand.Do you still remember the two questions for homework of the last period?The first one was, Is the encyclopedia made God for children or for adults?What do you think, Lucas?I think it's for children.From the introduction part, I know the encyclopedia is from May's father.That bought his daughter a children's encyclopedia for her to read.Good guessing.What do you think, Joyce?We read through the three entries several times.I found the words easy to understand.We can also find colourful illustrations.They help us to understand the entries better.Most of the illustrations are cartoons.Children are interested in cartoons.Most encyclopedias for adults are black and white.Thank you, Joyce.You did a good job.Both Lucas and Joyce have found some evidence to prove that the encyclopedia is for children.Is there any more evidence?Let's read the entries again.First, the entry Dinosaurs.When read, please pay attention to how the writer describes the sizes of the dinosaurs.LukasSome were as small as chickens.Others were as big as ten elephants.Right.Can you imagine the sizes of small dinosaurs and big dinosaurs, Joyce?A chicken is about 30 to 40 cm tall.A small dinosaur seems to be really small.An elephant reaches over 2 meters.According to the sentence,A large dinosaur could reach almost 20 to 30 meters tall.It was huge.You got it.The writer uses these sentences to help children make a picture in mind.Children are not sensitive about numbers.They may not be able to have an image of the sizes of dinosaurs by reading numbers only.So here, the writer uses comparison to catch children's attention.The comparative structure as-as and then can help readers visualize an extinct animal species by comparing it with living animals.Can you translate these two sentences into Chinese?Some dinosaurs are as big as chickens, while others are as big as ten elephants.If May's father is an elephant, he could be as big as ten elephants.If May's father is reading an encyclopedia for information of dinosaurs, what will he probably read?Maybe he will read an entry like this.It is full of numbers.Adults are more sensitive about numbers.Both ways help us make pictures in mind.However, using as-as or then is a better way for children to understand.Can you find other sentences like this in this entry?They were as gentle as sheep and ate plants.They were fiercer than tigers.Good.These two sentences show how gentle and fierce some dinosaurs were.Now, let's move on to the entry of Diogenes.Diogenes had his own idea about happiness.What was it, Joyce?The way to be happy was to own as few things as possible.To help children understand Diogenes' idea, what does the writer do?Write a story about Diogenes.In Unit 4, in order to show how fast a human brain can be, the writer includes a story about a competition between Shakuntala Devi and a computer.Remember what we call the story about a real person or incident?Yes, it is called an anecdote.We use anecdote to support an opinion or the topic sentence.Good, Joyce.The story about Diogenes is also an anecdote.Then, why do we need anecdotes in encyclopedias for children?Joyce, what do you think?In the entry of Diogenes, his idea about happiness is quite different for children in modern world to understand.The writer uses the story to make it easy for us to understand.The story supports and explains the main idea of the entry.Sometimes, we need anecdotes to explain a difficult idea or theory, to provide background information.Sometimes, we use anecdotes to paint a clear and vivid picture for the readers.Thus, anecdotes are also necessary in children's encyclopedias.Why does the entry Da Vinci Leonardo talk about his paintings first but not his inventions?Which are you familiar with, his paintings or his inventions?I think most of you have heard of Mona Lisa.It is kept in the Louvre in Paris, France.Art lovers always dream of visiting the museum and seeing the painting, right?The writer first introduces his paintings, something you are more familiar with, then his notebook, full of new ideas, which you are not quite familiar with.This helps you make connections between them easily.You will find the entry easy to understand and interesting to read.To help children to understand, you need to read the book.To help children understand an entry, the writer always talks about things children are familiar with first.Now, please read the first sentence of the two entries, Da Vinci Leonardo and the Diogenes.What can you learn from them?They tell who they were.Both of the entries start with a definition.下定義也是百科全書中常見的寫作方法。In the introduction part, a brief definition is usually given at the beginning, followed by a main body of detailed descriptions.We cannot find that definition in the second entry.Can you give a definition to dinosaurs?This is the first question in task one on your worksheet.Maybe we can say, a dinosaur was an animal that lived over 60 million years ago, but no longer exists.Since we are learning about encyclopedias in this unit, can you give a definition to encyclopedias?Can you complete it?This is question two in task one.Lucas, please.An encyclopedia is a book that gives facts about different subjects.The entries in the book are usually arranged in alphabetical order.An encyclopedia often consists of a number of books.Each is called a volume.Very good, Lucas.Have you got the right answers?Now, let's move on.Till now, we have talked a lot about encyclopedias for children.Do you still remember the title of the text?That's Look It Up.What does look up mean?Yes, it means to look for information in a reference book.But here, the reference book we use is the encyclopedia.What does it in the title refer to?Is it the encyclopedia?I don't think so.You can say look it up in the encyclopedia.But you cannot say look the encyclopedia up.You are looking something up in the encyclopedia.Remember the entries?If it is the first time for you to read them, you don't know about them.You want to learn about them.So it refers to a topic that you don't know, am I right?Bingo, Jice.Here, it refers to any unfamiliar topic to you.What else do you use to look something up?You use dictionaries as well, right?We can either use a dictionary or an encyclopedia to look up dinosaurs.But can we get similar information?Now, please read the two entries.The one on the left is from the Online Oxford Dictionary.The one on the right is from your student's book.What are the differences?A dictionary entry only gives the definition about a word.But an encyclopedia entry tells us detailed facts.From the dictionary entry, we only know what a dinosaur is.That is the meaning of the word.But from the encyclopedia entry, we not only know what a dinosaur is, but also what it looked like, when and where it lived, how people learn about them nowadays, and many other facts.They are totally for different purposes.But both are very useful and necessary reference books.Diogenes thought the way to be happy was to own as few things as possible.Do you agree?Think about this question and share your opinions.Thank you for watching.Lukas, what's your view about the first question?No, I don't agree, because I grow up owning things.It might take me a long time to adjust to not owning anything.I found it very hard to live without a house or apartment.I like having a place to call my own, where I can rest and do things in private.What about you, Joyce?I agree, if you own fewer things, you don't have to take care of them.You will buy only the things you really need, and not too many of them.You can free up more time and money to spend on experiences with endless people.You really understand the meaning of Diogenes' idea about happiness.There is an old saying in China, content is happiness.We shouldn't ask for those things that are used to show off.You should be pleased with your life and put your heart into studying.Now, it's time to summer.In this class, we actually talked a lot about the characteristics of the encyclopedias for children.You'd better take down some notes in task two in your worksheet.Children's encyclopedias include easy words and vivid illustrations.To help children make a picture in mind, they often include comparative structures like SS or then.To make children interested in reading the entries, they sometimes have got anecdotes.To provide background information, to present images to the readers, the writers write about familiar things to children first.To make children better understand the entries, we give some further explanations if necessary.By doing these, children are able to understand the detailed effects in the entries.Have you noted them?Today's homework.You are asked to complete exercises D1 and D2 on page 77 of your student's book.You will also need to read two more encyclopedia entries and finish some reading tasks.This is the end of today's class.See you next time.
